prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1018; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A dated inspection photo shows the same dent before this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured's vehicle was changing lanes. The claimant reports a knee injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and two witnesses at the scene place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. Photos taken at the scene show some of the reported details, but no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 4: Reviewed the vehicle damage against the described impact. The dent pattern and paint transfer are consistent with a sideswipe from the adjacent lane.

Entry 5: Obtained a dated inspection photo from a prior service visit. It shows the same dent on the vehicle before this crash, which makes the earlier damage an open question I need to look into further.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant by phone. The account of how the collision happened matched the first statement given at the scene.

Entry 7: Reviewed the knee injury against the kind and force of the collision. The injury is a reasonable match for this type of impact.

Entry 8: Checked prior medical records. No earlier injury to the same body area is on file.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course, with visits tapering off as the claimant's knee improved. Records reflect steady recovery.

Entry 10: The claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far. Based on the current file, the claim is ready for coverage review and a settlement recommendation, with the prior dent photo still needing a follow-up.
